name: MiniLLM: On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
authors: Gu, Li, Liu, Zhu, Zhou, Chen, Lin, Sui
problem: Distilling a WHITE-BOX LLM into a smaller LLM is under-explored - most KD work either distills classifiers or only imitates a black-box API - and forward KL lets the student waste capacity imitating low-probability regions of the teacher.
mechanism: Two changes. (1) REVERSE Kullback-Leibler divergence instead of forward KL: forward KL is mass-covering and makes the student spread probability over the teacher's low-probability tails, which is exactly the wrong inductive bias for sequence generation. Reverse KL is mode-seeking and yields a sharper, more precise student. (2) An ON-POLICY optimization derivation that makes this objective trainable - the student samples its own outputs and is scored against the teacher on those, removing the train/inference distribution mismatch.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): students generate MORE PRECISE RESPONSES with higher overall quality, LOWER EXPOSURE BIAS, BETTER CALIBRATION, and higher long-text generation performance than the baselines, in the instruction-following setting. No numeric accuracy delta or speedup ratio appears in the abstract. 'Better calibration' is the underrated claim here: a well-calibrated student does not need to be retrained before it can be quantized or served under distribution shift.
